a2-105.scenario: Petra asks Meg what she has on at work today. You (Meg) are sending two emails today, and you have to write a report by the afternoon.
a2-105.prompt: Tell Petra what you are sending today and what you have to write by the afternoon.
cues: Say you are sending emails
Say you have to write a report by the afternoon
a2-105.target: Ma két e-mailt küldök. Délutánig egy jelentést kell írnom.
a2-105.english: Today I'm sending two emails. I have to write a report by this afternoon.
a2-105.canDo: I can talk about common work tasks like writing a report or sending an email.

a2-105-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: My Workday
a2-105-consolidation.scenario: Petra asks Meg about her job. You (Meg) work in an office, you work eight hours a day, and today you have to work again.
a2-105-consolidation.prompt: Tell Petra where you work, how many hours you work, and that you have to work today.
cues: Say where you work
Say how many hours a day you work
Say you have to work today
a2-105-consolidation.target: Egy irodában dolgozom. Naponta nyolc órát dolgozom, és ma is dolgoznom kell.
a2-105-consolidation.english: I work in an office. I work eight hours a day, and today I have to work too.
a2-105-consolidation.canDo: I can name common professions and say what my job is with X vagyok.

a2-106.title: Communicative Challenge: Into the Shop
a2-106.scenario: It is Saturday morning and Károly phones Meg while she is out shopping. You (Meg) are going into the shop now, and then you will come out of it.
a2-106.prompt: Tell Károly that you are going into the shop now and then coming out of it.
cues: Say you are going into the shop
Say you come out afterwards
a2-106.target: Most bemegyek a boltba. Aztán kijövök a boltból.
a2-106.english: I'm going into the shop now. Then I'll come out of the shop.
a2-106.canDo: I can say when someone goes in or comes out of a place using bemegy, bejön, kimegy, and kijön.

a2-107.title: Communicative Challenge: Getting Up
a2-107.scenario: Károly asks Meg about her Saturday morning. You (Meg) get up early, and then sit down on the chair for breakfast.
a2-107.prompt: Tell Károly that you get up early and then sit down on a chair.
cues: Say you get up early
Say you sit down on the chair
a2-107.target: Korán felkelek. Aztán leülök a székre.
a2-107.english: I get up early. Then I sit down on the chair.
a2-107.canDo: I can talk about getting up, sitting down, and lying down using felkel, lefekszik, leül, and felül.

a2-108.title: Communicative Challenge: Start and Finish
a2-108.scenario: Károly asks Meg when she starts and finishes work on Monday. You (Meg) start working at nine and finish work at five.
a2-108.prompt: Tell Károly when you start working on Monday and when you finish.
cues: Say when you start working
Say when you finish work
a2-108.target: Hétfőn kilenckor elkezdek dolgozni. Ötkor befejezem a munkát.
a2-108.english: On Monday at nine I start working. At five I finish work.
a2-108.canDo: I can say when I start and finish something using elkezd and befejez.

a2-109.title: Communicative Challenge: Getting It Done
a2-109.scenario: Károly asks Meg what she is doing next in the flat. You (Meg) get the task done first, then drink up your water.
a2-109.prompt: Tell Károly that you get the task done first, and then drink up the water.
cues: Say you get the task done
Say you drink up the water
a2-109.target: Megcsinálom a feladatot. Aztán megiszom a vizet.
a2-109.english: I'll get the task done. Then I'll drink up the water.
a2-109.canDo: I can say I get something completely done using megcsinál.

a2-110.title: Communicative Challenge: Not Yet
a2-110.scenario: Károly asks Meg about her plans for the morning. You (Meg) get up at seven and go into the shop, but you are not eating up the soup yet.
a2-110.prompt: Tell Károly that you get up at seven and go into the shop, and that you are not eating up the soup yet.
cues: Say you get up and go into the shop
Say you are not eating the soup up yet
a2-110.target: Hétkor felkelek, és bemegyek a boltba. Aztán megeszem a levest.
a2-110.english: I get up at seven and go into the shop. Then I eat up the soup.
a2-110.canDo: I can keep a verb prefix glued to the front of the verb in a plain statement.

a2-110-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Cleaning Day
a2-110-consolidation.scenario: Károly asks Meg what she is doing on cleaning day. Today you are not going into the shop, but you will get the task done, then sit down and drink up the water.
a2-110-consolidation.prompt: Tell Károly that you are not going into the shop today but you will get the task done, then sit down and drink up the water.
cues: Say you are not going into the shop but will get the task done
Say you will sit down and drink up the water
a2-110-consolidation.target: Ma nem megyek be a boltba, de megcsinálom a feladatot. Aztán leülök, és megiszom a vizet.
a2-110-consolidation.english: Today I'm not going into the shop, but I'll get the task done. Then I'll sit down and drink up the water.
a2-110-consolidation.canDo: I can use bemegy, bejön, kimegy, and kijön to say that someone goes in or comes out of a place.

a2-111.title: Communicative Challenge: What Can You Do?
a2-111.scenario: On the way to the local office to register her new address, Károly asks Meg what she can do. You (Meg) can drive and cook, but you play the piano badly.
a2-111.prompt: Tell Károly which skills you have, and which one you are bad at.
cues: Say what you can do
Say which skill you are bad at
a2-111.target: Tudok vezetni és főzni, de rosszul tudok zongorázni.
a2-111.english: I can drive and cook, but I play the piano badly.
a2-111.canDo: I can talk about a wider range of skills using tud, like driving, cooking, and playing an instrument.

a2-112.title: Communicative Challenge: I Can't Drive
a2-112.scenario: Károly asks Meg to drive them to the office. You (Meg) can't drive because you are still learning, and today you wouldn't be able to drive anyway because it is raining.
a2-112.prompt: Tell Károly that you can't drive because you are still learning, and that today you can't drive because it is raining.
cues: Say you can't drive and why
Say that today it isn't possible to drive and why
a2-112.target: Nem tudok vezetni, mert még tanulok. Ma nem lehet vezetni, mert esik az eső.
a2-112.english: I can't drive, because I'm still learning. Today you can't drive, because it's raining.
a2-112.canDo: I can say I'm not able to do something and explain why using nem tud + infinitive and mert.

a2-113.title: Communicative Challenge: Is It Possible?
a2-113.scenario: At the local office Meg asks the clerk what is possible. You (Meg) ask whether you can park here and whether you can pay by card here.
a2-113.prompt: Ask the clerk if it is possible to park here and if it is possible to pay by card.
cues: Ask whether it is possible to park
Ask whether it is possible to pay by card
a2-113.target: Elnézést, lehet itt parkolni? Lehet itt kártyával fizetni?
a2-113.english: Excuse me, is it possible to park here? Is it possible to pay by card here?
a2-113.canDo: I can ask whether something is possible using Lehet + infinitive, and answer with Igen, lehet / Nem, nem lehet.

a2-114.title: Communicative Challenge: Is It Allowed?
a2-114.scenario: At the office Meg asks the clerk whether photography is allowed, then points out to Károly a sign about smoking.
a2-114.prompt: Ask the clerk if it is allowed to take photographs here, then tell Károly that smoking is not allowed here.
cues: Ask whether photography is allowed
Say that smoking is not allowed
a2-114.target: Szabad itt fényképezni? Itt nem szabad dohányozni.
a2-114.english: Is it allowed to take photographs here? You must not smoke here.
a2-114.canDo: I can ask and say what's allowed by a rule using szabad + infinitive.

a2-115.title: Communicative Challenge: What Can We Do?
a2-115.scenario: After the office Károly asks Meg what they can do today. You (Meg) can cycle, it is possible to cycle in the park today, and it is allowed there.
a2-115.prompt: Tell Károly that you can cycle, that today it is possible in the park, and that it is allowed.
cues: Say you are able to cycle
Say it is possible and allowed in the park today
a2-115.target: Tudok biciklizni. Ma lehet a parkban biciklizni, és szabad is.
a2-115.english: I can cycle. Today it's possible to cycle in the park, and it's allowed too.
a2-115.canDo: I can combine tud, lehet, and szabad in one conversation about plans, choosing the right one for ability, possibility, or permission.

a2-115-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Rules and Skills
a2-115-consolidation.scenario: Károly asks Meg to help with the car. You (Meg) cook well, but you can't drive because you are still learning, and parking is not allowed here.
a2-115-consolidation.prompt: Tell Károly that you cook well but can't drive because you are still learning, and that you must not park here.
cues: Say what you do well and what you can't do
Say what is not allowed here
a2-115-consolidation.target: Jól tudok főzni, de nem tudok vezetni, mert még tanulok. Itt nem szabad parkolni.
a2-115-consolidation.english: I can cook well, but I can't drive, because I'm still learning. You must not park here.
a2-115-consolidation.canDo: I can talk about skills using tud, and grade them with jól/rosszul.

a2-116.title: Communicative Challenge: Yesterday
a2-116.scenario: Károly gets home late and asks Meg about her first day at the new job. You (Meg) worked a lot yesterday and studied in the evening.
a2-116.prompt: Tell Károly that you worked a lot yesterday and that you studied in the evening.
cues: Say you worked a lot yesterday
Say you studied in the evening
a2-116.english: I worked a lot yesterday. In the evening I studied.
a2-116.canDo: I can form the past tense of regular verbs in all persons (indefinite conjugation).

a2-117.title: Communicative Challenge: Last Weekend
a2-117.scenario: Károly asks Meg what she and her friends did last weekend. You (Meg) went hiking in the morning and then had a picnic in the park.
a2-117.prompt: Tell Károly that last weekend you went hiking in the morning and then had a picnic in the park.
cues: Say you went hiking last weekend
Say you then had a picnic in the park
a2-117.target: Múlt hétvégén reggel kirándultunk, aztán piknikeztünk a parkban.
a2-117.english: Last weekend we hiked in the morning, then had a picnic in the park.
a2-117.canDo: I can talk about weekend activities in the past tense using kirándul, piknikezik and sportol.

a2-118.title: Communicative Challenge: What Did You Do?
a2-118.scenario: Károly asks Meg what she did all day at work, and who she talked to. You (Meg) talked to your boss and had lunch with Petra, and then ask Károly what he did.
a2-118.prompt: Tell Károly who you talked to and who you had lunch with, and ask what he did.
cues: Say whom you talked to
Say whom you had lunch with
Ask what he did
a2-118.target: Beszéltem a főnökömmel, és Petrával ebédeltem. Te mit csináltál?
a2-118.english: I talked to my boss, and I had lunch with Petra. What did you do?
a2-118.canDo: I can ask and answer past-tense questions like Mit csináltál? and Kivel beszéltél?

a2-119.title: Communicative Challenge: Where Were You?
a2-119.scenario: Károly asks Meg where she was at eight o'clock yesterday morning. You (Meg) were already at the office, and you ask him where he was.
a2-119.prompt: Tell Károly that you were already at the office at eight yesterday morning, and ask where he was.
cues: Say where you were and when
Ask where he was
a2-119.target: Tegnap reggel nyolckor már az irodában voltam. Hol voltál te?
a2-119.english: Yesterday morning at eight I was already at the office. Where were you?
a2-119.canDo: I can use volt, the past tense of van, in all persons.

a2-120.title: Communicative Challenge: Bus, Soup and Coffee
a2-120.scenario: Károly asks Meg to tell him about her day. You (Meg) went to the office by bus, had soup at noon, and drank a coffee.
a2-120.prompt: Tell Károly how you went to the office and what you had at noon.
cues: Say how you went to the office
Say what you ate and drank at noon
a2-120.target: Busszal mentem az irodába. Délben levest ettem, és kávét ittam.
a2-120.english: I went to the office by bus. At noon I ate soup and drank coffee.
a2-120.canDo: I can use the past tense of megy and jön (ment, jött) in all persons.

a2-120-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: My First Day
a2-120-consolidation.scenario: Károly asks Meg to tell the story of her first day at the new job. You (Meg) got up early yesterday morning and were at the office, then had soup at noon and worked a lot.
a2-120-consolidation.prompt: Tell Károly the story of your first day: what you did in the morning, at noon and afterwards.
cues: Say what you did in the morning
Say what you ate at noon
Say what you did afterwards
a2-120-consolidation.target: Tegnap reggel korán felkeltem, és az irodában voltam. Délben levest ettem, aztán sokat dolgoztam.
a2-120-consolidation.english: Yesterday morning I got up early and was at the office. At noon I ate soup, then I worked a lot.
a2-120-consolidation.canDo: I can form the past tense of regular verbs, indefinite and definite, in all persons.

a2-121.title: Communicative Challenge: The Coat from the Window
a2-121.scenario: Károly notices your new coat at the office. You (Meg) bought a coat yesterday, and it is the one that was in the shop window.
a2-121.prompt: Tell Károly that you bought a coat yesterday, and that you finally bought the one from the shop window.
cues: Say you bought a coat yesterday
Say you finally bought the specific coat from the window
a2-121.target: Tegnap vettem egy kabátot. Végül megvettem a kabátot, ami a kirakatban volt.
a2-121.english: Yesterday I bought a coat. In the end I bought the coat that was in the shop window.
a2-121.canDo: I can say what I bought using vettem (something) vs. megvettem (that specific thing).

a2-122.title: Communicative Challenge: Who Did You Meet?
a2-122.scenario: In the evening you (Meg) tell Károly about your day: you ran into Tamás at the market by chance. You also want to know who Károly met.
a2-122.prompt: Tell Károly that you met Tamás at the market by chance, then ask whom he met today.
cues: Say you met Tamás by chance
Say where you met him
Ask whom Károly met today
a2-122.target: Véletlenül találkoztam Tamással a piacon. Kivel találkoztál ma?
a2-122.english: I met Tamás by chance at the market. Who did you meet today?
a2-122.canDo: I can say who I met using találkozik + -val/-vel, and ask Kivel találkoztál?

a2-123.title: Communicative Challenge: A Gift for Ildikó
a2-123.scenario: Károly asks you (Meg) what you bought for Ildikó's birthday. You bought a beautiful vase, and you also bought the expensive gift that he asked about earlier.
a2-123.prompt: Tell Károly that you bought a beautiful vase for Ildikó, and that you bought the expensive gift he asked about.
cues: Say you bought a beautiful vase for Ildikó
Say you bought the expensive gift he asked about
a2-123.target: Vettem egy gyönyörű vázát Ildikónak. Megvettem a drága ajándékot.
a2-123.english: I bought a beautiful vase for Ildikó. I bought the expensive gift.
a2-123.canDo: I can describe what I bought or saw with an adjective, keeping the adjective bare and putting the case ending only on the noun.

a2-124.title: Communicative Challenge: What Happened to the Coat?
a2-124.scenario: Károly bought a new coat. You (Meg) want to know what happened to his old one. You also sold your own old bag last week.
a2-124.prompt: Ask Károly what he did with the old coat, then say that you sold your old bag.
cues: Ask what he did with the old coat
Say you sold your old bag
a2-124.target: Mit csináltál a régi kabáttal? Eladtam a régi táskámat.
a2-124.english: What did you do with the old coat? I sold my old bag.
a2-124.canDo: I can ask and answer Mit csináltál vele? about something I bought, found, or met.

a2-125.title: Communicative Challenge: My Day in Order
a2-125.scenario: Károly asks Meg about her day. You (Meg) bought the gift for Ildikó, met Tamás at the market, and then went home.
a2-125.prompt: Tell Károly your day in order: you bought the gift, you met Tamás, and after that you went home.
cues: Say you bought the gift
Say you then met Tamás
Say what you did after that
a2-125.target: Megvettem az ajándékot, aztán találkoztam Tamással. Utána hazamentem.
a2-125.english: I bought the gift, then I met Tamás. After that I went home.
a2-125.canDo: I can connect several past-tense events with aztán and utána.

a2-125-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: This Morning
a2-125-consolidation.scenario: Petra asks Meg what she did this morning. You (Meg) had a coffee, met Tamás by chance, and later bought a gift for Ildikó.
a2-125-consolidation.prompt: Tell Petra what you did this morning: you drank a coffee, met Tamás by chance, and later bought a gift for Ildikó.
cues: Say what you drank
Say whom you met by chance
Say what you bought later and for whom
a2-125-consolidation.target: Reggel ittam egy kávét, aztán véletlenül találkoztam Tamással. Később vettem egy ajándékot Ildikónak.
a2-125-consolidation.english: In the morning I drank a coffee, then I met Tamás by chance. Later I bought a gift for Ildikó.
a2-125-consolidation.canDo: I can talk about things I did in the past, like Reggel ittam egy kávét.

a2-126.title: Communicative Challenge: Late and Lost
a2-126.scenario: Tamás asks why you (Meg) were late this morning. Your car broke down, and you also lost your key, but luckily you found it later.
a2-126.prompt: Tell Tamás that your car broke down so you were late, and that you lost your key but luckily found it.
cues: Say your car broke down, so you were late
Say you lost your key
Say you found it luckily
a2-126.target: Sajnos elromlott az autóm, ezért elkéstem. Elveszítettem a kulcsomat, de szerencsére megtaláltam.
a2-126.english: Unfortunately my car broke down, so I was late. I lost my key, but luckily I found it.
a2-126.canDo: I can say I was late for something using elkésik, and that I lost something using elveszít.

a2-127.title: Communicative Challenge: The Joke
a2-127.scenario: At the party Zsófia asks why you (Meg) were laughing so much. Károly told a very funny joke.
a2-127.prompt: Tell Zsófia that you laughed a lot at the joke, and that Károly told a funny story.
cues: Say you laughed a lot
Say what you laughed at
Say who told the funny story
a2-127.target: Nagyon nevettem a viccen. Károly elmesélt egy vicces történetet.
a2-127.english: I laughed a lot at the joke. Károly told a funny story.
a2-127.canDo: I can say I laughed, and what I laughed at, using nevet + the superessive case.

a2-128.title: Communicative Challenge: Last Summer in Vienna
a2-128.scenario: Zsófia asks Meg about her last trip. You (Meg) traveled to Vienna with Károly last summer, and the weather there was gorgeous.
a2-128.prompt: Tell Zsófia that you traveled to Vienna with Károly last summer, and that the weather was gorgeous when you were there.
cues: Say where you traveled, with whom and when
Say what the weather was like while you were there
a2-128.target: Tavaly nyáron Bécsbe utaztunk Károllyal. Amikor Bécsben voltunk, gyönyörű volt az idő.
a2-128.english: Last summer we traveled to Vienna with Károly. When we were in Vienna, the weather was gorgeous.
a2-128.canDo: I can talk about a past trip using utazik.

a2-129.title: Communicative Challenge: Rain in the Park
a2-129.scenario: Tamás asks what happened on your (Meg's) walk in the park. You were walking with Petra when it suddenly started to rain, and Petra said it was very funny.
a2-129.prompt: Tell Tamás that you were walking in the park when suddenly it started to rain, and that Petra said it was very funny.
cues: Say you were walking in the park
Say it suddenly started to rain
Report what Petra said
a2-129.target: Sétáltunk a parkban, amikor egyszer csak elkezdett esni. Petra azt mondta, hogy nagyon vicces volt.
a2-129.english: We were walking in the park when all of a sudden it started to rain. Petra said that it was very funny.
a2-129.canDo: I can describe a surprising event using egyszer csak or váratlanul with elkezd and an infinitive.

a2-130.title: Communicative Challenge: The Whole Trip
a2-130.scenario: Anna asks Meg to tell the story of her trip in one go. At the beginning it rained, then you (Meg) walked around the city, and at the end the weather was gorgeous.
a2-130.prompt: Tell Anna the story of your trip: at the beginning it rained, then you walked around, and at the end the weather was gorgeous.
cues: Say what the weather was like at the beginning
Say what you did next
Say what the weather was like at the end
a2-130.target: Az elején esett az eső, aztán sétáltunk, de a végén gyönyörű volt az idő.
a2-130.english: At the beginning it rained, then we walked around, but at the end the weather was gorgeous.
a2-130.canDo: I can frame a story using az elején and a végén, alongside the sequencing words I already know.

a2-130-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: A Bad Weekend
a2-130-consolidation.scenario: Petra asks Meg about her weekend. You (Meg) were late for work, then lost your key, but luckily Károly spotted it.
a2-130-consolidation.prompt: Tell Petra that unfortunately you were late for work and lost your key, but luckily Károly spotted it.
cues: Say you were late for work
Say you lost your key
Say luckily Károly spotted it
a2-130-consolidation.target: Sajnos elkéstem a munkából, aztán elveszítettem a kulcsomat. Szerencsére Károly meglátta.
a2-130-consolidation.english: Unfortunately I was late for work, then I lost my key. Luckily Károly spotted it.
a2-130-consolidation.canDo: I can narrate a day that went wrong using elkésik, elveszít, sajnos, and szerencsére.

a2-131.title: Communicative Challenge: Tomorrow's Plans
a2-131.scenario: Petra asks you (Meg) what you and Károly are doing tomorrow. You have a lot of work, and Károly will be studying.
a2-131.prompt: Tell Petra what you will do tomorrow, and what Károly will do.
cues: Say that you will work a lot tomorrow
Say that Károly will study tomorrow
a2-131.target: Holnap sokat fogok dolgozni. Károly holnap fog tanulni.
a2-131.english: Tomorrow I will work a lot. Károly will study tomorrow.
a2-131.canDo: I can build the future tense with fog and a plain infinitive, for I/you/he/she.

a2-132.title: Communicative Challenge: Next Week
a2-132.scenario: Petra asks you (Meg) about next week. You and Károly will work a lot, and you want to know whether Petra and her friends will travel.
a2-132.prompt: Tell Petra that you and Károly will work a lot next week, then ask whether she and her friends will travel.
cues: Say what you and Károly will do next week
Ask whether Petra and her friends will travel
a2-132.target: Jövő héten sokat fogunk dolgozni. Ti fogtok utazni?
a2-132.english: Next week we will work a lot. Will you (pl.) travel?
a2-132.canDo: I can conjugate fog + infinitive for we/you (pl.)/they, as well as I/you/he/she.

a2-133.title: Communicative Challenge: Career Plans
a2-133.scenario: Károly asks you (Meg) about your career. You are planning to look for a new job, and you are only possibly thinking about a promotion.
a2-133.prompt: Tell Károly what you are planning, and what you are only thinking about.
cues: Say what you are planning to do
Say what you are possibly thinking about
a2-133.target: Tervezek egy új állást keresni. Esetleg gondolkodom egy előléptetésen.
a2-133.english: I'm planning to look for a new job. I'm possibly thinking about a promotion.
a2-133.canDo: I can say what I'm planning to do using tervez + infinitive.

a2-134.title: Communicative Challenge: The Weekend
a2-134.scenario: Károly has a free weekend. You (Meg) want to know what he will do, and you tell him you will not be working.
a2-134.prompt: Ask Károly what he will do this weekend, and say that you won't work.
cues: Ask what Károly will do at the weekend
Say that you will not work
a2-134.target: Mit fogsz csinálni a hétvégén? Én nem fogok dolgozni.
a2-134.english: What will you do this weekend? I won't work.
a2-134.canDo: I can ask what someone will do using fog + infinitive.

a2-135.title: Communicative Challenge: Visiting Ildikó and Gábor
a2-135.scenario: Petra asks you (Meg) about next week. You and Károly are visiting Ildikó and Gábor, it is already arranged. You expect to talk a lot with them, and you are planning to rest a lot.
a2-135.prompt: Tell Petra about next week: what is fixed, what you expect, and what you are planning.
cues: Say what is already arranged
Say what you expect will happen
Say what you are planning to do
a2-135.target: Jövő héten meglátogatjuk Ildikót és Gábort. Valószínűleg sokat fogunk beszélni. Tervezünk sokat pihenni.
a2-135.english: Next week we're visiting Ildikó and Gábor. We'll probably talk a lot. We're planning to rest a lot.
a2-135.canDo: I can pick the right construction — present tense, fog, or tervez — for what I want to say about the future.

a2-135-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Who Will Do What
a2-135-consolidation.scenario: Károly asks who will do what tomorrow. You (Meg) will work, Petra and Gábor will rest, and you and Károly will not travel.
a2-135-consolidation.prompt: Tell Károly what you will do, what Petra and Gábor will do, and what the two of you won't do.
cues: Say what you will do tomorrow
Say what Petra and Gábor will do
Say what you and Károly will not do
a2-135-consolidation.target: Holnap én dolgozni fogok. Petra és Gábor pihenni fognak. Mi nem fogunk utazni.
a2-135-consolidation.english: Tomorrow I will work. Petra and Gábor will rest. We won't travel.
a2-135-consolidation.canDo: I can build the future tense with fog and a plain infinitive, for all six persons.

a2-136.title: Communicative Challenge: Cinema Tonight
a2-136.scenario: It is Saturday evening and you (Meg) are at home with Károly. You would like to go to the cinema and then eat something together.
a2-136.prompt: Suggest to Károly that you go to the cinema tonight, and then eat something.
cues: Suggest going to the cinema tonight
Suggest eating something afterwards
a2-136.target: Menjünk moziba ma este? Aztán együnk valamit?
a2-136.english: Shall we go to the cinema tonight? Then shall we eat something?
a2-136.canDo: I can suggest doing something together using the -junk/-jünk imperative as a question.

a2-137.title: Communicative Challenge: What I Would Do
a2-137.scenario: Károly asks what you (Meg) would do this evening. You are hungry and tired.
a2-137.prompt: Tell Károly what you would eat, and that you would stay home.
cues: Say what you would eat
Say that you would stay home
a2-137.english: I would eat something. I would stay at home.
a2-137.canDo: I can say what I would do by adding -nék to a verb, as in szeretnék, várnék and tanulnék.

a2-138.title: Communicative Challenge: A Sore Back
a2-138.scenario: Károly has worked all day and says his back hurts. You (Meg) are worried about him.
a2-138.prompt: Tell Károly that he should rest more and that he should go to the doctor.
cues: Say that Károly should rest more
Say that he should go to the doctor
a2-138.target: Neked kellene többet pihenni. Neked kellene orvoshoz menni.
a2-138.english: You should rest more. You should go to the doctor.
a2-138.canDo: I can aim advice at a specific person using neked/neki kellene.

a2-139.title: Communicative Challenge: A Free Day
a2-139.scenario: Károly asks what you (Meg) would do on a free day, what he would do, and what the two of you would do together.
a2-139.prompt: Tell Károly what you would do, what he would do, and what the two of you would do. You would stay home and read, he would go for a walk, and you would watch a film.
cues: Say what you would do
Say what Károly would do
Say what the two of you would do
a2-139.target: Én otthon maradnék és olvasnék. Te sétálnál. Mi filmet néznénk.
a2-139.english: I would stay home and read. You would go for a walk. We would watch a film.
a2-139.canDo: I can conjugate a regular verb in the conditional for every person, not just I and you.

a2-140.title: Communicative Challenge: If It Weren't Raining
a2-140.scenario: It is raining and Károly wants to go to the park. You (Meg) have a lot of work and no free time.
a2-140.prompt: Tell Károly what you would do if it weren't raining, and what you would do if you had time.
cues: Say what you would do if it weren't raining
Say what you would do if you had time
a2-140.target: Ha nem esne, sétálnánk egyet a parkban. Ha lenne időm, elmennék moziba.
a2-140.english: If it weren't raining, we would take a walk in the park. If I had time, I would go to the cinema.
a2-140.canDo: I can build a hypothetical "if" sentence using ha with the conditional in both clauses.

a2-140-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: A Film Tonight
a2-140-consolidation.scenario: Meg and Károly are at home in the evening. You (Meg) would like to watch a film with Károly, but you don't care which one.
a2-140-consolidation.prompt: Suggest watching a film tonight and say that it doesn't matter to you which one.
cues: Suggest watching a film together
Say that you don't mind which one
a2-140-consolidation.target: Nézzünk egy filmet ma este? Nekem mindegy, melyiket.
a2-140-consolidation.english: Shall we watch a film tonight? I don't mind which one.
a2-140-consolidation.canDo: I can suggest doing something together using the -junk/-jünk imperative as a question, and react to a suggestion.

a2-141.title: Communicative Challenge: Giving My Opinion
a2-141.scenario: Petra asks you (Meg) what you think of Károly's idea. Károly looks tired after a long day.
a2-141.prompt: Tell Petra you think it is a good idea, and guess that Károly is tired.
cues: Give your opinion about the idea
Make a guess about Károly
a2-141.target: Azt hiszem, ez jó ötlet. Károly fáradt, gondolom.
a2-141.english: I think this is a good idea. Károly is tired, I guess.
a2-141.canDo: I can introduce an opinion with szerintem, azt hiszem, or gondolom.

a2-142.title: Communicative Challenge: Tea or Coffee
a2-142.scenario: At the café Károly asks if you (Meg) want coffee, and then asks about tonight.
a2-142.prompt: Tell Károly you would rather drink tea than coffee, and that you would rather stay at home tonight.
cues: Say what you would rather drink than coffee
Say what you would rather do tonight
a2-142.target: Inkább teát iszom, mint kávét. Ma este inkább otthon maradok.
a2-142.english: I'd rather drink tea than coffee. Tonight I'd rather stay at home.
a2-142.canDo: I can say what I'd rather do with inkább, and what I'd rather do than something else.

a2-143.title: Communicative Challenge: Which Restaurant Is Better
a2-143.scenario: You (Meg) and Petra are choosing between the Italian restaurant and the Chinese restaurant for tonight.
a2-143.prompt: Ask Petra which restaurant is better, and say the Italian one is better than the Chinese one.
cues: Ask which restaurant is better
Compare the two restaurants
a2-143.target: Melyik étterem jobb? Az olasz étterem jobb, mint a kínai.
a2-143.english: Which restaurant is better? The Italian restaurant is better than the Chinese one.
a2-143.canDo: I can compare two named things, like restaurants or films, and ask which one is better.

a2-144.title: Communicative Challenge: I Don't Agree
a2-144.scenario: Károly says the new restaurant is better. You (Meg) disagree, but Petra thinks the same as you.
a2-144.prompt: Tell Károly you don't agree with him, and that you agree with Petra.
cues: Say you don't agree with Károly
Say you agree with Petra
a2-144.target: Nem értek egyet veled. Egyetértek Petrával.
a2-144.english: I don't agree with you. I agree with Petra.
a2-144.canDo: I can say I agree or disagree with someone using egyetért and nem értek egyet.

a2-145.title: Communicative Challenge: Why the New Job
a2-145.scenario: Petra asks you (Meg) which job is better. The new job is more exciting.
a2-145.prompt: Tell Petra which job is better in your opinion and give a reason.
cues: Say which job is better in your opinion
Give a reason
a2-145.target: Szerintem az új munka jobb, mert izgalmasabb.
a2-145.english: In my opinion the new job is better, because it is more exciting.
a2-145.canDo: I can back up an opinion with a reason using mert.

a2-145-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Which Restaurant Tonight
a2-145-consolidation.scenario: Petra asks which restaurant is better for tonight, the Italian or the Chinese. Károly said the Italian one, and it is cheaper.
a2-145-consolidation.prompt: Give your opinion about the better restaurant, say why, and say you agree with Károly.
cues: Give your opinion about the better restaurant
Give a reason
Say you agree with Károly
a2-145-consolidation.target: Szerintem az olasz étterem jobb, mert olcsóbb. Egyetértek Károllyal.
a2-145-consolidation.english: In my opinion the Italian restaurant is better, because it is cheaper. I agree with Károly.
a2-145-consolidation.canDo: I can give my opinion with szerintem, azt hiszem or gondolom.

a2-146.title: Communicative Challenge: My Job and My Morning
a2-146.scenario: Zsófia asks you (Meg) about your job and your workday.
a2-146.prompt: Tell Zsófia that you work for a company, and that you set off in the morning and start work at nine.
cues: Say who you work for
Say what you do in the morning
a2-146.target: Egy cégnél dolgozom. Reggel elindulok, kilenckor elkezdek dolgozni.
a2-146.english: I work for a company. In the morning I set off, at nine I start working.
a2-146.canDo: I can talk about my job, where I work, and my workday, using possessive suffixes and cases.

a2-147.title: Communicative Challenge: Piano Yes, Swimming No
a2-147.scenario: Anna asks you (Meg) if you can play the piano and if you can swim. You play well, but you never learned to swim.
a2-147.prompt: Tell Anna that you can play the piano well, and that you can't swim because you never learned.
cues: Say what you can do well
Say what you can't do and why
a2-147.target: Jól tudok zongorázni. Nem tudok úszni, mert sosem tanultam.
a2-147.english: I can play the piano well. I can't swim, because I never learned.
a2-147.canDo: I can say what I'm able to do, and explain why I can't, using tud + infinitive.

a2-148.title: Communicative Challenge: What I Did Yesterday
a2-148.scenario: Károly asks what you (Meg) did yesterday. You worked in the morning, met Zsófia, and in the afternoon you bought a coat.
a2-148.prompt: Tell Károly that you worked in the morning and then met Zsófia, and that you bought a coat in the afternoon.
cues: Say what you did in the morning, then who you met
Say what you bought in the afternoon
a2-148.target: Reggel dolgoztam, aztán találkoztam Zsófiával. Délután egy kabátot vettem.
a2-148.english: In the morning I worked, then I met Zsófia. In the afternoon I bought a coat.
a2-148.canDo: I can talk about what I did, ate, drank, bought, saw and where I was, using the past tense with the definite/indefinite distinction.

a2-149.title: Communicative Challenge: Next Weekend
a2-149.scenario: Anna asks you (Meg) what you are doing at the weekend. You won't work, and you plan to rest.
a2-149.prompt: Tell Anna that you won't work at the weekend, and that you plan to rest a lot.
cues: Say that you won't work
Say what you plan to do
a2-149.target: Nem fogok dolgozni a hétvégén. Tervezek sokat pihenni.
a2-149.english: I won't work at the weekend. I plan to rest a lot.
a2-149.canDo: I can talk about the future with fog + infinitive, tervez + infinitive, and majd, and negate the future.

a2-150.title: Communicative Challenge: Not the Italian Restaurant
a2-150.scenario: Zsófia says the Italian restaurant is better than the Chinese one. You (Meg) disagree, because the Chinese restaurant is cheaper.
a2-150.prompt: Tell Zsófia that you don't agree, and give your opinion with a reason.
cues: Say that you disagree
Give your opinion and a reason
a2-150.target: Nem értek egyet, mert szerintem a kínai étterem olcsóbb.
a2-150.english: I don't agree, because in my opinion the Chinese restaurant is cheaper.
a2-150.canDo: I can give my opinion, say what I prefer, compare things, and agree or disagree, backing it up with a reason.

a2-150-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Last Week and Tomorrow
a2-150-consolidation.scenario: Károly asks you (Meg) about yesterday and about tomorrow. You worked a lot yesterday, and tomorrow you will probably rest.
a2-150-consolidation.prompt: Tell Károly that you worked a lot yesterday, and that you will probably rest tomorrow.
cues: Say what you did yesterday
Say what you will probably do tomorrow
a2-150-consolidation.target: Tegnap sokat dolgoztam. Holnap valószínűleg pihenni fogok.
a2-150-consolidation.english: Yesterday I worked a lot. Tomorrow I will probably rest.
a2-150-consolidation.canDo: I can use the main vocabulary and grammar from Units 21-29.

a2-151.title: Communicative Challenge: What Is Broken
a2-151.scenario: Károly asks you (Meg) what is wrong in the flat. The heating broke, and the wifi does not work.
a2-151.prompt: Tell Károly that the heating broke and that the wifi doesn't work.
cues: Say what broke
Say what doesn't work
a2-151.target: Elromlott a fűtés. Nem működik a wifi.
a2-151.english: The heating broke. The wifi doesn't work.
a2-151.canDo: I can report that something doesn't work or broke, using nem működik and elromlott.

a2-152.title: Communicative Challenge: Could You Help
a2-152.scenario: You (Meg) meet the mechanic at the door. You need help with the heating, and you must ask politely, as to a stranger.
a2-152.prompt: Politely ask the mechanic if he could help, and say that you need help.
cues: Ask politely, to a stranger, if he could help
Say that you need help
a2-152.target: Elnézést, tudna segíteni? Szükségem van segítségre.
a2-152.english: Excuse me, could you help? I need help.
a2-152.canDo: I can politely ask someone if they could help me, using tudna/tudnál segíteni.

a2-153.title: Communicative Challenge: A Faulty Product
a2-153.scenario: You (Meg) bought a product that does not work. The seller asks what the problem is.
a2-153.prompt: Tell the seller that you want to complain because the product doesn't work, and ask for a refund.
cues: Open the complaint and give the reason
Ask for a refund
a2-153.target: Szeretnék reklamálni, mert nem működik a termék. Kérek egy visszatérítést.
a2-153.english: I'd like to complain, because the product doesn't work. I'd like a refund.
a2-153.canDo: I can make a complaint and explain the problem, using szeretnék reklamálni.

a2-154.title: Communicative Challenge: Phoning the Doctor
a2-154.scenario: Károly asks you (Meg) about tomorrow. You will phone the doctor, and you want to change an appointment.
a2-154.prompt: Tell Károly that you will phone the doctor tomorrow, and that you'd like to change an appointment.
cues: Say what you will do tomorrow
Say that you want to change an appointment
a2-154.target: Holnap fogok telefonálni az orvosnak. Szeretnék módosítani egy időpontot.
a2-154.english: Tomorrow I will phone the doctor. I'd like to change an appointment.
a2-154.canDo: I can talk about the future using fog + infinitive.

a2-155.title: Communicative Challenge: The Heating Is Fixed
a2-155.scenario: The heating broke. You (Meg) phone the mechanic, who answers politely.
a2-155.prompt: Tell the mechanic that the heating broke and that you therefore need help, and ask him politely if he could come today.
cues: Say what broke and that you need help
Ask politely if he could come today
a2-155.target: Elromlott a fűtés, ezért szükségem van segítségre. Tudna ma jönni?
a2-155.english: The heating broke, so I need help. Could you come today?
a2-155.canDo: I can describe a problem, ask for help, and get it solved in one connected exchange.

a2-155-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: At the Hotel Desk
a2-155-consolidation.scenario: At the hotel desk the receptionist asks you (Meg) what the problem is. In your room the air conditioning doesn't work and a towel is missing.
a2-155-consolidation.prompt: Tell the receptionist what doesn't work and what is missing, and politely ask if they could help.
cues: Say what doesn't work and what is missing
Ask politely, to a stranger, if they could help
a2-155-consolidation.target: Nem működik a klíma, és hiányzik egy törölköző. Tudna segíteni?
a2-155-consolidation.english: The air conditioning doesn't work, and a towel is missing. Could you help?
a2-155-consolidation.canDo: I can report that something doesn't work or broke, using nem működik and elromlott, and say something is missing, using hiányzik.

a2-156.title: Communicative Challenge: A Whole Day
a2-156.scenario: Petra, a new colleague, asks Meg what an ordinary day looks like. You (Meg) get up at seven, shower and have breakfast, work from nine to five, and have dinner in the evening.
a2-156.prompt: Tell Petra about your day, from the morning to the evening, linking the parts with time words.
cues: Say when you get up and what you do first and then
Say when you work
Finish with what you do in the evening
a2-156.target: Hétkor felkelek, előbb zuhanyozom, aztán reggelizem. Kilenctől ötig dolgozom, végül este vacsorázom.
a2-156.english: I get up at seven, first I shower, then I have breakfast. I work from nine to five, and finally in the evening I have dinner.
a2-156.canDo: I can describe a whole day in Hungarian, from morning to night, linking the parts with time words.

a2-157.title: Communicative Challenge: My Family and Home
a2-157.scenario: Petra asks Meg about her family. Your parents live in a small house with a nice garden, and your younger brother rents a flat on the third floor.
a2-157.prompt: Tell Petra where your parents live and what your younger brother is doing now.
cues: Say where your parents live and what is there
Say what your younger brother is doing now and where
a2-157.target: A szüleim egy kis házban laknak, ahol szép kert van. Az öcsém most bérel egy lakást a harmadik emeleten.
a2-157.english: My parents live in a small house where there is a nice garden. My younger brother is renting a flat on the third floor now.
a2-157.canDo: I can talk about my family, friends and home together in fuller, more natural sentences.

a2-158.title: Communicative Challenge: From Market to Pot
a2-158.scenario: Károly asks Meg what she did yesterday afternoon. You (Meg) went to the market to buy onion and meat, then cooked goulash at home.
a2-158.prompt: Tell Károly what you bought at the market and what you did with it at home.
cues: Say what you bought and where
Say what you did with it at home
a2-158.target: A piacon hagymát és húst vásároltam. Otthon felvágtam a hagymát, és megfőztem a gulyást.
a2-158.english: At the market I bought onion and meat. At home I cut up the onion, and cooked the goulash.
a2-158.canDo: I can describe going shopping for ingredients and cooking a meal, from market to table.

a2-159.title: Communicative Challenge: My Work Day
a2-159.scenario: Ildikó asks Meg what her working week is like. Your working hours start at eight and end at five, you often have meetings with your colleagues, and there are a lot of tasks.
a2-159.prompt: Tell Ildikó about a typical work day: your hours, your colleagues and your tasks.
cues: Say when your working hours start and end
Say what you often have with your colleagues
Say how much work there is
a2-159.target: Hétköznap nyolckor kezdődik a munkaidőm, és ötkor végződik. A munkatársaimmal gyakran van megbeszélésünk, és sok a feladat.
a2-159.english: On weekdays my working hours start at eight and end at five. I often have meetings with my colleagues, and there are a lot of tasks.
a2-159.canDo: I can describe a work day in detail, using colleagues, tasks and my schedule together.

a2-160.title: Communicative Challenge: The Heating Broke Down
a2-160.scenario: It is a cold evening and Meg is at home with Károly. The heating in the flat has stopped working, and you cannot fix it yourself.
a2-160.prompt: Tell Károly what is wrong and ask him politely if he could help.
cues: Say what has broken down
Say it does not work
Ask politely for help
a2-160.target: Elromlott a fűtés, nem működik. Tudnál segíteni?
a2-160.english: The heating broke down, it doesn't work. Could you help?
a2-160.canDo: I can explain what's wrong when something breaks or stops working, and ask politely for help.

a2-160-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: What I Did Yesterday
a2-160-consolidation.scenario: Petra asks Meg what she did yesterday. You (Meg) got up early, worked, and went home in the evening.
a2-160-consolidation.prompt: Tell Petra what you did yesterday, from the morning to the evening, using time words to link your actions.
cues: Say what you did first in the morning
Say what you did next
Say how the day ended
a2-160-consolidation.target: Tegnap reggel korán felkeltem, aztán dolgoztam, végül hazamentem.
a2-160-consolidation.english: Yesterday morning I got up early, then I worked, and finally I went home.
a2-160-consolidation.canDo: I can describe a whole day in Hungarian, and tell someone what I did, using several actions and time connectors together.

a2-161.title: Communicative Challenge: Do You Trust Me?
a2-161.scenario: Károly asks Meg whether she trusts him, and whether she is sure that Anna will come to the party tonight.
a2-161.prompt: Answer both of Károly's questions: say that you trust him, and that you are sure of it.
cues: Say that you trust him
Say that you are sure of it
a2-161.target: Bízom benned, és biztos vagyok benne.
a2-161.english: I trust you, and I am sure of it.
a2-161.canDo: I can use inessive personal pronouns (bennem, benned, benne...) accurately.

a2-162.title: Communicative Challenge: Your Turn
a2-162.scenario: Meg, Károly and Anna are playing a game at home. Károly is hesitating and cannot decide what to do.
a2-162.prompt: Tell Károly that it is his turn and that the decision is up to him.
cues: Say that it is his turn
Say that the decision depends on him
a2-162.target: Most rajtad van a sor, és a döntés is rajtad múlik.
a2-162.english: Now it is your turn, and the decision is up to you too.
a2-162.canDo: I can use superessive personal pronouns (rajtam, rajtad, rajta...) in context.

a2-163.title: Communicative Challenge: Wait for Me
a2-163.scenario: Meg is going to be late. Károly is already at the station and is waiting. You phone him.
a2-163.prompt: Ask Károly to wait for you at the station, and say that you often think of him.
cues: Ask him to wait for you at the station
Say that you often think of him
a2-163.target: Kérlek, várj rám az állomáson! Sokat gondolok rád.
a2-163.english: Please wait for me at the station! I think of you a lot.
a2-163.canDo: I can use sublative personal pronouns (rám, rád, rá...) with verbs of direction, waiting, and thought.

a2-164.title: Communicative Challenge: You Can Count on Me
a2-164.scenario: Anna is nervous before an important presentation. You (Meg) sit next to her and want to support her.
a2-164.prompt: Tell Anna that you trust her, that she can count on you, and that it all depends on her.
cues: Say that you trust her
Say that she can count on you
Say that it all depends on her
a2-164.target: Bízom benned, és számíthatsz rám. Minden rajtad múlik.
a2-164.english: I trust you, and you can count on me. It all depends on you.
a2-164.canDo: I can contrast inessive, superessive, and sublative personal pronouns.

a2-165.title: Communicative Challenge: Before the Exam
a2-165.scenario: Károly has an important exam tomorrow and is very nervous. You (Meg) are with him.
a2-165.prompt: Encourage Károly: tell him not to be nervous, that you trust him, and that you are thinking of him.
cues: Tell him not to be nervous
Say that you trust him
Say that you are thinking of him
a2-165.target: Ne izgulj, bízom benned! Gondolok rád.
a2-165.english: Don't be nervous, I trust you! I am thinking of you.
a2-165.canDo: I can offer encouragement and moral support using declined pronouns.

a2-165-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: A Quiz Evening
a2-165-consolidation.scenario: Meg, Károly and Anna are at a family quiz evening. Károly is next, and he is nervous.
a2-165-consolidation.prompt: Tell Károly that you trust him, that you are waiting for him, and that it is his turn.
cues: Say that you trust him
Say that you are waiting for him
Say that it is his turn
a2-165-consolidation.target: Bízom benned, rád várok, és most rajtad van a sor.
a2-165-consolidation.english: I trust you, I am waiting for you, and now it is your turn.
a2-165-consolidation.canDo: I can use inessive, superessive and sublative personal pronouns.

a2-166.title: Communicative Challenge: Who Has the Key?
a2-166.scenario: Meg, Károly and Anna are about to leave the flat. Anna asks who has the umbrella and who has the key. You (Meg) have the umbrella, and Károly has the key.
a2-166.prompt: Tell Anna that you have the umbrella, and that Károly is the one who has the key.
cues: Say that you have the umbrella
Say that Károly has the key
a2-166.target: Az esernyő nálam van, a kulcs pedig nála.
a2-166.english: The umbrella is with me, and the key is with him.
a2-166.canDo: I can use adessive pronouns (nálam, nálad, nála...) to say who has an item right now.

a2-167.title: Communicative Challenge: Come Over to My Place
a2-167.scenario: You (Meg) want to invite Anna to your place on Saturday. Mariann is coming too.
a2-167.prompt: Invite Anna to your place on Saturday and tell her that Mariann is coming over as well.
cues: Invite her to your place on Saturday
Say that Károly is coming over too
a2-167.target: Gyere el hozzám szombaton! Mariann is átjön hozzám.
a2-167.english: Come over to my place on Saturday! Károly is coming over to my place too.
a2-167.canDo: I can use allative personal pronouns (hozzám, hozzád, hozzá...) to invite people over.

a2-168.title: Communicative Challenge: Asking Péter for Help
a2-168.scenario: Meg is visiting Péter. She needs help with her homework and has no pen.
a2-168.prompt: Ask Péter whether you can ask him for help, and whether you can borrow a pen from him.
cues: Ask if you can ask him for help
Ask if you can borrow a pen from him
a2-168.target: Kérhetek tőled segítséget? Kölcsönkérhetek tőled egy tollat?
a2-168.english: Can I ask you for help? Can I borrow a pen from you?
a2-168.canDo: I can use ablative personal pronouns (tőlem, tőled, tőle...) with verbs of requesting, receiving, and departing.

a2-169.title: Communicative Challenge: What Did They Say About Me?
a2-169.scenario: Meg meets Péter for the first time. Péter says that Károly has told him a lot about her.
a2-169.prompt: Tell Péter that you have heard a lot about him as well, and ask what they said about you.
cues: Say you have also heard a lot about him
Ask what they said about you
a2-169.target: Én is sokat hallottam rólad. Mit mondtak rólam?
a2-169.english: I have heard a lot about you too. What did they say about me?
a2-169.canDo: I can use delative personal pronouns (rólam, rólad, róla...) to discuss people and topics.

a2-170.title: Communicative Challenge: Dinner at Károly's
a2-170.scenario: Mariann and Péter have invited Meg and Anna for dinner. Meg arrives, and Mariann welcomes her at the door.
a2-170.prompt: Thank Mariann and Péter politely, and say that you always like going to their place.
cues: Thank them and say it is kind of them
Say that you always like going to their place
a2-170.target: Nagyon kedves tőletek, köszönöm! Mindig szívesen megyek hozzátok.
a2-170.english: That is very kind of you, thank you! We always like going to your place.
a2-170.canDo: I can interact naturally as a guest or host using the proximity pronoun system.

a2-170-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: The Recipe Is at My Place
a2-170-consolidation.scenario: Anna wants to cook goulash but does not know the recipe. You (Meg) have the recipe at home.
a2-170-consolidation.prompt: Tell Anna that the recipe is at your place, invite her over tonight, say that she can ask you for help, and that you will tell her everything about it.
cues: Say where the recipe is
Invite her over tonight
Say she can ask you for help
Say you will tell her everything about it
a2-170-consolidation.target: A recept nálam van, gyere át hozzám ma este! Kérj tőlem segítséget, és mindent elmesélek róla.
a2-170-consolidation.english: The recipe is at my place, come over to my place tonight! Ask me for help, and I will tell you everything about it.
a2-170-consolidation.canDo: I can use the pronouns nál-, hozzá-, től- and ról- to say at, to, from and about a person.

a2-171.title: Communicative Challenge: After the Winter
a2-171.scenario: Carlos visits Zoltán at his family home in District VIII after a long winter. Zoltán (you) catches him up on what changed.
a2-171.prompt: Tell Carlos what happened to the snow in front of the house, and what your daughter became.
cues: Say what the snow turned into in front of the house
Say what your daughter became
a2-171.target: A hó vízzé olvadt a ház előtt. A lányom orvossá vált.
a2-171.english: The snow melted into water in front of the house. My daughter became a doctor.
a2-171.canDo: I can form the translative-factitive case (-vá / -vé) with vowel stems.

a2-172.title: Communicative Challenge: The Dream Came True
a2-172.scenario: Carlos and Zoltán have a coffee in District VIII; the plan for Zoltán's old storage room has finally been approved. Zoltán (you) says what has happened to his dream and to the two of you.
a2-172.prompt: Tell Carlos that your dream finally became reality and that you two became good friends.
cues: Say what your dream became
Say what the two of you became
a2-172.target: Az álmom végre valósággá vált. Mi jó barátokká váltunk.
a2-172.english: My dream finally became reality. We became good friends.
a2-172.canDo: I can conjugate and use 'válik' with the translative case.

a2-173.title: Communicative Challenge: A Machine for the Workshop
a2-173.scenario: Carlos brings good news and a new machine to Zoltán's workshop. Zoltán (you) tells him what the news and the machine do.
a2-173.prompt: Tell Carlos that the news made you happy and that the machine makes the work easier.
cues: Say what the news did to you
Say what the machine does to the work
a2-173.target: Ez a hír boldoggá tett. A gép könnyebbé teszi a munkát.
a2-173.english: This news made me happy. The machine makes the work easier.
a2-173.canDo: I can use 'tesz' with translative adjectives to express causation (making something X).

a2-174.title: Communicative Challenge: A Cold Morning
a2-174.scenario: Carlos and Zoltán wait outside the old storage room on a winter morning, and Carlos asks what the night was like. Zoltán (you) answers.
a2-174.prompt: Tell Carlos that the water froze into ice and that the sky turned dark before the storm.
cues: Say what the water turned into
Say what happened to the sky before the storm
a2-174.target: A víz jéggé fagyott, és az ég sötétté vált a vihar előtt.
a2-174.english: The water froze into ice, and the sky turned dark before the storm.
a2-174.canDo: I can talk about natural changes of state such as freezing, melting, and burning.

a2-175.title: Communicative Challenge: The Opening Evening
a2-175.scenario: On Friday evening Carlos and Zoltán stand in the new workshop and look at the finished room. Zoltán (you) tells Carlos how he feels.
a2-175.prompt: Tell Carlos that your shared dream finally came true and that surprise almost froze you like stone.
cues: Say what your shared dream became at last
Say how surprise nearly made you freeze
a2-175.target: Az álmunk végre valósággá vált. A meglepetéstől szinte kővé dermedtem.
a2-175.english: Our dream finally came true. I almost froze like stone from surprise.
a2-175.canDo: I can use idioms with the translative case such as 'valósággá válik' and 'kővé dermed'.

a2-175-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: What Changed
a2-175-consolidation.scenario: On the last day of the renovation Carlos asks Zoltán to sum up what changed. Zoltán (you) answers.
a2-175-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos what the old workshop became and that the work made the house prettier.
cues: Say what the old workshop became
Say what the work made prettier
a2-175-consolidation.target: A régi műhely kávézóvá vált. A munka szebbé tette a házat.
a2-175-consolidation.english: The old workshop became a café. The work made the house prettier.
a2-175-consolidation.canDo: I can use the translative-factitive case (-vá / -vé) accurately with verbs of becoming and making.

a2-176.title: Communicative Challenge: Who Does What at the Camp
a2-176.scenario: Carlos and Eszter have just arrived at the youth camp in Zebegény. Eszter asks Carlos (you) what he does for a living and how he helps at the camp.
a2-176.prompt: Tell Eszter what you work as, and that in the summer you help at the camp as a volunteer.
cues: Say what you work as
Say how you help at the camp in the summer
a2-176.target: Tanárként dolgozom, de a nyáron önkéntesként segítek a táborban.
a2-176.english: I work as a teacher, but in the summer I help at the camp as a volunteer.
a2-176.canDo: I can use the invariant suffix -ként to express roles and capacities.

a2-177.title: Communicative Challenge: Camps Then and Now
a2-177.scenario: Eszter asks Carlos (you) whether a summer camp is new to him, while the children play outside in Zebegény.
a2-177.prompt: Tell Eszter that you were often at camp as a child, and that as an adult you already help as a volunteer.
cues: Say what you did often as a child
Say how you help at camp as an adult
a2-177.target: Gyerekként sokat voltam táborban. Felnőttként már önkéntesként segítek.
a2-177.english: As a child I was at camp a lot. As an adult I already help as a volunteer.
a2-177.canDo: I can describe stages of life using 'gyerekként' and 'felnőttként'.

a2-178.title: Communicative Challenge: A Book for Eszter
a2-178.scenario: On the last evening at the camp Carlos (you) wants to thank Eszter, and he has a book for her.
a2-178.prompt: Give Eszter the book, and say it is a gift and a keepsake of the camp.
cues: Say you brought the book as a gift
Say it is a keepsake of the camp
a2-178.target: Ezt a könyvet ajándékként hoztam neked, emlékként a táborról.
a2-178.english: I brought you this book as a gift, as a keepsake of the camp.
a2-178.canDo: I can describe the intended function or purpose of objects using -ként.

a2-179.title: Communicative Challenge: Getting to the Camp
a2-179.scenario: Eszter's friend wants to visit the camp in Zebegény, and Eszter asks Carlos (you) how to get there.
a2-179.prompt: Tell Eszter how often the bus leaves for the camp and what a ticket costs per person.
cues: Say how often the bus leaves for the camp
Say what the ticket costs per person
a2-179.target: A busz óránként indul a táborba, és a jegy fejenként kétezer forintba kerül.
a2-179.english: The bus leaves for the camp every hour, and the ticket costs two thousand forints per person.
a2-179.canDo: I can use temporal adverbs like 'időnként' and 'naponként'.

a2-180.title: Communicative Challenge: Teacher, Volunteer, Future Doctor
a2-180.scenario: At the campfire in Zebegény, Eszter asks Carlos (you) about his job, his role at the camp and his family.
a2-180.prompt: Tell Eszter that you are a teacher but help at the camp as a volunteer, and that your daughter is studying to be a doctor.
cues: Say what you are
Say how you help at the camp
Say what your daughter is studying to become
a2-180.target: Tanár vagyok, de a táborban önkéntesként segítek. A lányom orvosnak tanul.
a2-180.english: I am a teacher, but at the camp I help as a volunteer. My daughter is studying to be a doctor.
a2-180.canDo: I can contrast -ként, -nak/-nek, and nominative predicate constructions.

a2-180-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Back at the Camp
a2-180-consolidation.scenario: On the way home Eszter asks Carlos (you) why this camp means so much to him.
a2-180-consolidation.prompt: Tell Eszter that you were often at this camp as a child and that now you help as a volunteer from time to time.
cues: Say what you did often at this camp as a child
Say how you help now from time to time
a2-180-consolidation.target: Gyerekként sokat voltam ebben a táborban, most időnként önkéntesként segítek.
a2-180-consolidation.english: As a child I was at this camp a lot, now I help as a volunteer from time to time.
a2-180-consolidation.canDo: I can use -ként for professions, stages of life, and purposes.

a2-181.title: Communicative Challenge: Greeting Eszter's Grandmother
a2-181.scenario: Carlos arrives at Eszter's grandmother's house in Szentendre. She is standing in the doorway and looks a little tired.
a2-181.prompt: Greet Eszter's grandmother respectfully, ask how she is, and offer her a seat.
cues: Greet her and use the word for grandmother
Ask politely how she is doing
Offer her a seat politely
a2-181.target: Jó napot kívánok, nagymama! Hogy tetszik lenni? Tessék, le tetszik ülni?
a2-181.english: Good day, grandma! How are you doing? Here you go, would you like to sit down?
a2-181.canDo: I can use the polite 'tetszik + infinitive' form to address elderly people respectfully.

a2-182.title: Communicative Challenge: Where Is the Post Office?
a2-182.scenario: Carlos wants to post a card to Eszter's grandmother. He stops a passer-by in Szentendre and wants to ask the way to the post office.
a2-182.prompt: Ask the passer-by politely to tell you where the post office is, and thank them.
cues: Ask the stranger politely (formal)
Ask where the post office is
Thank them
a2-182.target: Legyen szíves megmondani, merre van a posta! Köszönöm szépen!
a2-182.english: Would you please tell me where the post office is? Thank you very much!
a2-182.canDo: I can use 'tessék' and 'kérem' appropriately in service and public settings.

a2-183.title: Communicative Challenge: Introducing Yourself the Hungarian Way
a2-183.scenario: At the name-day lunch, Eszter's friend Katalin Horváth meets Ilona néni, Eszter's grandmother, for the first time. You are Katalin.
a2-183.prompt: Greet Ilona néni politely and introduce yourself with your family name first.
cues: Greet her politely
Say your name, family name first
Say whose friend you are
a2-183.target: Jó napot kívánok! Horváth Katalin vagyok, Eszter barátnője.
a2-183.english: Good day! I am Katalin Horváth, Eszter's friend.
a2-183.canDo: I can introduce myself using the Hungarian Eastern name order (family name first).

a2-184.title: Communicative Challenge: Ilona Néni's Name Day
a2-184.scenario: It is Ilona néni's name day. Carlos is standing with Eszter at the table, and everyone raises a glass to the grandmother.
a2-184.prompt: Congratulate Ilona néni on her name day, wish her a long life, and toast to her health.
cues: Wish her a happy name day
Wish her a long life
Toast to her health
a2-184.target: Boldog névnapot kívánok, nagymama! Isten éltessen sokáig! Egészségedre!
a2-184.english: I wish you a happy name day, grandma! May God grant you a long life! To your health!
a2-184.canDo: I can congratulate someone on their Name Day (névnap) using traditional greetings.

a2-185.title: Communicative Challenge: Guest Slippers and Lunch
a2-185.scenario: Carlos has taken off his shoes in the hall. Ilona néni gives him guest slippers, and then lunch is served at the table.
a2-185.prompt: Thank Ilona néni for the guest slippers and wish everyone a good meal.
cues: Thank her for the slippers
Wish everyone a good meal
a2-185.target: Köszönöm a vendégpapucsot! Jó étvágyat kívánok mindenkinek!
a2-185.english: Thank you for the guest slippers! Enjoy your meal, everyone!
a2-185.canDo: I understand Hungarian home visiting etiquette (taking off shoes, gifts, guest slippers).

a2-185-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Welcoming Grandma
a2-185-consolidation.scenario: Eszter's grandmother comes into the room where Carlos is waiting. He wants to be respectful and friendly.
a2-185-consolidation.prompt: Greet Eszter's grandmother respectfully, ask how she is, and wish her a good meal.
cues: Greet her respectfully
Ask how she is doing
Wish her a good meal
a2-185-consolidation.target: Jó napot kívánok, nagymama! Hogy tetszik lenni? Jó étvágyat kívánok!
a2-185-consolidation.english: Good day, grandma! How are you doing? Enjoy your meal!
a2-185-consolidation.canDo: I can use deferential politeness (tetszikelés) and public polite formulas.

a2-187.title: Communicative Challenge: Before Eszter's Exam
a2-187.scenario: Eszter is nervous about an important exam in Debrecen. Carlos phones her the evening before.
a2-187.prompt: Tell Eszter that you know her well, that you support her in everything, and that you will call her tomorrow.
cues: Say you know her well
Say you support her in everything
Say you will call her tomorrow
a2-187.target: Jól ismerlek, mindenben támogatlak. Holnap hívlak!
a2-187.english: I know you well, I support you in everything. I will call you tomorrow!
a2-187.canDo: I can apply vowel harmony with -lak and -lek.

a2-188.title: Communicative Challenge: A Bad Line at the Station
a2-188.scenario: Carlos is at the Nyugati station and phones Eszter, but the line is bad and she is hard to hear. He wants to wait for her at the entrance.
a2-188.prompt: Tell Eszter that you cannot hear her well and do not understand her, and that you will wait for her at the entrance.
cues: Say you cannot hear her well
Say you do not understand her
Say you will wait for her at the entrance
a2-188.target: Nem hallak jól, nem értelek. Megvárlak a bejáratnál.
a2-188.english: I can't hear you well, I don't understand you. I will wait for you at the entrance.
a2-188.canDo: I can negate verbs with -lak/-lek accurately.

a2-189.title: Communicative Challenge: Tea After the Journey
a2-189.scenario: Eszter has just arrived at the Nyugati station after a long journey and looks tired. A café is nearby.
a2-189.prompt: Invite Eszter for a tea in the café and say that you will walk her home afterwards.
cues: Invite her for a tea
Say where you will go
Say you will walk her home afterwards
a2-189.target: Meghívlak egy teára a kávézóba. Utána hazakísérlek.
a2-189.english: I invite you for a tea in the café. Afterwards I will walk you home.
a2-189.canDo: I can invite friends and make social offers using meghívlak.

a2-190.title: Communicative Challenge: By the Big Clock
a2-190.scenario: Carlos is waiting on the platform at the Nyugati station. Eszter's train is coming in, and she calls him from the train.
a2-190.prompt: Tell Eszter that you are waiting by the big clock, that you will notice her at once, and that you will give her a hug.
cues: Say where you are waiting
Say you will notice her at once
Say you will give her a hug
a2-190.target: A nagy óra mellett várlak, azonnal észreveszlek. Megölellek!
a2-190.english: I am waiting for you by the big clock, I will notice you at once. I will give you a hug!
a2-190.canDo: I can use -lak/-lek in railway station and travel situations.

a2-190-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Listening to a Friend
a2-190-consolidation.scenario: After her long journey Eszter is upset about something. Carlos sits down with her at the station café.
a2-190-consolidation.prompt: Tell Eszter that you cannot hear her well because of the crowd, that you are listening to her, and that you will always support her.
cues: Say you cannot hear her well
Say you are listening to her
Say you will always support her
a2-190-consolidation.target: Nem hallak jól, de hallgatlak. Mindig támogatlak.
a2-190-consolidation.english: I can't hear you well, but I am listening. I always support you.
a2-190-consolidation.canDo: I can conjugate and use verbs with the -lak/-lek suffix confidently.

a2-191.title: Communicative Challenge: Who Is Coming?
a2-191.scenario: Lili and Bálint are packing for the trip to the Balaton. You are Bálint. Lili asks who is coming along and whether your keys are in your bag.
a2-191.prompt: Answer Lili: tell her that your friends and your parents are coming, and that your keys are in your bag.
cues: Say who is coming
Say where your keys are
a2-191.target: A barátaim és a szüleim jönnek. A kulcsaim a táskámban vannak.
a2-191.english: My friends and my parents are coming. My keys are in my bag.
a2-191.canDo: I can use plural possessed nouns for my own things, such as barátaim, könyveim and kulcsaim (-aim, -eim).

a2-192.title: Communicative Challenge: Where Are Your Things?
a2-192.scenario: Bálint and Lili are waiting at the station when Máté arrives without his bags. You are Bálint and you speak to Máté.
a2-192.prompt: Ask Máté where his things are, and tell him that Lili's parents are already here.
cues: Ask where his things are
Say that Lili's parents are already here
a2-192.target: Hol vannak a dolgaid? Lili szülei már itt vannak.
a2-192.english: Where are your things? Lili's parents are already here.
a2-192.canDo: I can say your friends (barátaid) and his/her friends (barátai) with -aid/-eid and -ai/-ei.

a2-193.title: Communicative Challenge: Our Plans for the Balaton
a2-193.scenario: Máté phones Lili and Bálint to ask who is coming to the Balaton and what the plans are. You are Lili and you answer for you and Bálint.
a2-193.prompt: Tell Máté that your friends and your parents are coming too, and that your plans are very exciting.
cues: Say who else is coming
Say what you think of your plans
a2-193.target: A barátaink és a szüleink is jönnek. A terveink nagyon izgalmasak.
a2-193.english: Our friends and our parents are coming too. Our plans are very exciting.
a2-193.canDo: I can form and use plural possessed forms for plural owners (-aink/-eink, -aitok/-eitek, -aik/-eik).

a2-194.title: Communicative Challenge: A Present for My Parents
a2-194.scenario: Máté meets Bálint at the station and asks about the weekend. You are Bálint.
a2-194.prompt: Tell Máté who you are travelling to the Balaton with, and that you bought a present for your parents.
cues: Say who you are travelling with
Say who the present is for
a2-194.target: A barátaimmal utazom a Balatonra. A szüleimnek ajándékot vettem.
a2-194.english: I am travelling to the Balaton with my friends. I bought a present for my parents.
a2-194.canDo: I can attach instrumental (-val/-vel), dative (-nak/-nek), and spatial cases to plural possessed nouns.

a2-195.title: Communicative Challenge: Whose Suitcase?
a2-195.scenario: At the door of the flat, Lili asks Máté (you) whether the tickets and documents are with him, and whose suitcase is standing by the door.
a2-195.prompt: Answer Lili: tell her that your tickets and documents are in your pocket, and that the suitcase is not yours but Bálint's.
cues: Say where your tickets and documents are
Say whose suitcase it is
a2-195.target: A jegyeim és az irataim a zsebemben vannak. A bőrönd nem az enyém, hanem Bálinté.
a2-195.english: My tickets and my documents are in my pocket. The suitcase is not mine, it is Bálint's.
a2-195.canDo: I can use plural possessed nouns of all persons with the accusative and other endings.

a2-195-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Ready to Go
a2-195-consolidation.scenario: Before leaving the flat, Lili asks Bálint (you) who he is travelling with and where he put his keys.
a2-195-consolidation.prompt: Answer Lili: say that you are travelling with your friends and your parents, and that you put your keys into your bag.
cues: Say who you are travelling with
Say where you put your keys
a2-195-consolidation.target: A barátaimmal és a szüleimmel utazom. A kulcsaimat a táskámba tettem.
a2-195-consolidation.english: I am travelling with my friends and my parents. I put my keys into my bag.
a2-195-consolidation.canDo: I can use plural possessed nouns for all persons, with the endings of this unit (-aim, -eid, -ai, -eink, -eitek, -eik).

a2-196.title: Communicative Challenge: In the Queue
a2-196.scenario: Máté and Anna are in a long queue at the ticket office in the Castle District. Anna has just arrived and asks Máté (you) how the queue looks.
a2-196.prompt: Tell Anna that a tall man is standing in front of you and that she is standing behind you.
cues: Say who is standing in front of you
Say where Anna is standing
a2-196.target: Előttem áll egy magas férfi, mögöttem te állsz.
a2-196.english: A tall man is standing in front of me, you are standing behind me.
a2-196.canDo: I can inflect spatial postpositions with personal suffixes (előttem, mögötted, mellette).

a2-197.title: Communicative Challenge: Noisy Neighbours
a2-197.scenario: Anna is telling Máté about her flat in Budapest. You are Anna and you complain about the noise upstairs.
a2-197.prompt: Tell Máté that the neighbours live right above you (and your family), and ask him to keep it between the two of you.
cues: Say where the neighbours live
Ask him to keep it secret
a2-197.target: A szomszédok pontosan felettünk laknak. Ez maradjon köztünk!
a2-197.english: The neighbours live right above us. Let this stay between us!
a2-197.canDo: I can use inflected vertical and relational postpositions (alattam, felettünk, köztünk).

a2-198.title: Communicative Challenge: Don't Go Without Me
a2-198.scenario: Máté and Anna are about to leave the café in the Castle District, but Máté (you) still has to pay. Anna is already standing up.
a2-198.prompt: Ask Anna not to leave without you, and tell her that your colleague is working instead of you this evening.
cues: Ask her not to leave without you
Say who is working instead of you
a2-198.target: Kérlek, ne menj el nélkülem! Ma este a kollégám dolgozik helyettem.
a2-198.english: Please, don't leave without me! Tonight my colleague is working instead of me.
a2-198.canDo: I can use inflected forms of nélkül (nélkülem, nélküled) and helyett (helyettem, helyette).

a2-199.title: Communicative Challenge: Don't Worry About Me
a2-199.scenario: Máté has missed his train and phones Anna from the station. You are Máté and Anna is worried.
a2-199.prompt: Tell Anna not to worry about you and that your brother is coming to the station by car to pick you up.
cues: Reassure Anna
Say who is coming to pick you up and how
a2-199.target: Ne aggódj miattam! A bátyám autóval kijön értem az állomásra.
a2-199.english: Don't worry about me! My brother is coming out to the station by car to pick me up.
a2-199.canDo: I can use miattam, miattad (because of me, you) and értem, érted (for me, you).

a2-200.title: Communicative Challenge: Follow Me
a2-200.scenario: Anna shows Máté the way through the busy streets of the Castle District. You are Anna and you lead the way.
a2-200.prompt: Tell Máté to follow you, and then to sit down next to you on the bench for a rest.
cues: Tell him to follow you
Tell him to sit down next to you
a2-200.target: Gyere utánam! Ülj le mellém a padra, pihenjünk egy kicsit!
a2-200.english: Follow me! Sit down beside me on the bench, let's rest a bit!
a2-200.canDo: I can use position and movement forms such as mellettem and mellém, előttem and elém, and utánam.

a2-200-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Meet Me at the Station
a2-200-consolidation.scenario: Máté phones Anna while she is leaving the Castle District. You are Máté and you arrive by train later.
a2-200-consolidation.prompt: Ask Anna not to leave without you, and tell her that your friend is coming to meet you at the station.
cues: Ask her not to leave without you
Say who is coming to meet you
a2-200-consolidation.target: Ne menj el nélkülem! A barátom elém jön az állomásra.
a2-200-consolidation.english: Don't leave without me! My friend is coming to meet me at the station.
a2-200-consolidation.canDo: I can use the inflected postpositions of this unit (előttem, nélkülem, helyettem, miattam, utánam).

a2-201.title: Communicative Challenge: I Have to Go
a2-201.scenario: Monday morning: Dániel is hurrying out of the kitchen while Nóra is still having coffee. You are Dániel.
a2-201.prompt: Tell Nóra that you have to go now and that she has to study a lot tonight.
cues: Say that you have to go now
Say that Nóra has to study a lot tonight
a2-201.target: Most már mennem kell. Neked ma este sokat kell tanulnod.
a2-201.english: I have to go now. You have to study a lot tonight.
a2-201.canDo: I can form inflected infinitives across all six persons (mennem, tanulnod, főznie, mennünk, mennetek, tanulniuk).

a2-202.title: Communicative Challenge: No Need to Hurry
a2-202.scenario: Nóra and Dániel are leaving a restaurant. Dániel looks at his watch and starts to rush. You are Nóra.
a2-202.prompt: Tell Dániel that he does not have to hurry because there is still enough time, and that you have to get up early tomorrow.
cues: Say that he does not have to hurry
Say what you have to do tomorrow
a2-202.target: Nem kell sietned, van még elég időnk. Holnap korán fel kell kelnem.
a2-202.english: You don't have to hurry, we still have enough time. Tomorrow I have to get up early.
a2-202.canDo: I can express obligation and urgency using kell and muszáj with inflected infinitives.

a2-203.title: Communicative Challenge: May I Come In?
a2-203.scenario: Dániel stands at his boss's office door in the morning. You are Dániel and the boss has not answered yet.
a2-203.prompt: Politely ask whether you may come into the office for a moment and whether you may ask a question.
cues: Ask to come in
Ask politely to ask a question
a2-203.target: Szabad bejönnöm egy pillanatra az irodába? Szabadna kérdeznem egyet?
a2-203.english: May I come into the office for a moment? May I ask a question?
a2-203.canDo: I can ask for permission politely using szabad and szabadna with inflected infinitives.

a2-204.title: Communicative Challenge: Worth Leaving Early
a2-204.scenario: Over breakfast Nóra asks Dániel how his day looks. You are Dániel.
a2-204.prompt: Tell Nóra that it is worth her leaving early, and that yesterday you had to work late in the office.
cues: Give Nóra advice
Say what you had to do yesterday
a2-204.target: Érdemes korán elindulnod. Tegnap sokáig kellett dolgoznom az irodában.
a2-204.english: It's worth you leaving early. Yesterday I had to work late in the office.
a2-204.canDo: I can use evaluative predicates (érdemes, felesleges, nehéz, jó) with inflected infinitives.

a2-205.title: Communicative Challenge: Sorry, I Am Busy
a2-205.scenario: Nóra invites Dániel (you) for lunch this Friday, but he has a deadline.
a2-205.prompt: Politely tell Nóra that you have no time today because you have to finish a report, and that you have to hand it in by Friday.
cues: Politely decline
Say what you have to finish
Say the deadline
a2-205.target: Sajnos nem érek rá, mert be kell fejeznem a jelentést. Péntekig le kell adnom.
a2-205.english: Unfortunately I have no time, because I have to finish the report. I have to hand it in by Friday.
a2-205.canDo: I can manage a complete weekly schedule with deadlines, appointments, and obligations using inflected infinitives.

a2-205-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Time to Go Home
a2-205-consolidation.scenario: Dániel and Nóra are at a friend's dinner and it is getting late. You are Nóra and you speak for both of you.
a2-205-consolidation.prompt: Thank the hosts for the evening and say that you have to go home now and that you have to get up early tomorrow.
cues: Thank the hosts
Say that you have to go home
Say that you have to get up early
a2-205-consolidation.target: Köszönöm a szép estét, de sajnos most már haza kell mennünk. Holnap korán kell kelnünk.
a2-205-consolidation.english: Thank you for the nice evening, but unfortunately we have to go home now. Tomorrow we have to get up early.
a2-205-consolidation.canDo: I can use inflected infinitives with kell, muszáj, szabad, lehet and érdemes.

a2-206.title: Communicative Challenge: At the Counter
a2-206.scenario: Péter has just come into the district post office. He has taken a queue ticket, and the display now calls his number to window three, where the clerk is waiting.
